nodes.label: Next.js
nodes.rationale: No external API, no serverless-functions requirement, no build step outside next build — runs anywhere Node.js + MySQL are available, which is what makes Namecheap hosting a workable target.

nodes.label: Custom JWT Auth
nodes.rationale: Custom JWT cookies (jsonwebtoken + bcryptjs) used instead of a third-party auth service; JWT_SECRET must use a different value in production than in local dev for security.

nodes.label: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Fully custom admin panel under /admin built from the same Next.js app, avoiding a separate third-party CMS/dashboard dependency.

nodes.label: public/uploads/ Storage
nodes.rationale: Excluded from git (.gitignore) since it is runtime data, not source code; must be backed up and preserved across redeploys.

nodes.label: storage/private/ Storage
nodes.rationale: Deliberately kept outside public/ so paid files can never be downloaded via a direct URL, only through the signed /api/downloads route after verifying the buyer paid.

nodes.label: public/sw.js Service Worker
nodes.rationale: Only registers in production (npm run build && npm start) so it can be tested; PWA install only works on localhost or real HTTPS, not plain http://IP addresses.

nodes.label: Customer Area, Affiliate & Payments
nodes.rationale: Payments are manual: buyer sends money and enters a Transaction ID, which an admin verifies in Admin -> Orders before marking it PAID.

nodes.label: server.js (Passenger Adapter)
nodes.rationale: Next.js's own server doesn't speak cPanel's Passenger protocol directly, so this tiny server.js is shipped at the project root just for that; Passenger sets process.env.PORT itself.
